title: North Shore Club 北濱會
content_html: The North Shore Club is a rotating savings and social organization (標會) founded by Taiwanese American families living on Chicago’s North Shore. The group was established approximately in 1978 when around a dozen Taiwanese American households lived in the area, with children of preschool and elementary school age. Its primary purpose is fellowship and monthly communal dining, with the rotating savings (標會) function serving as a secondary activity. Monthly gatherings were traditionally held potluck-style at the home of the winning bidder, where members socialized late into the night — men often discussing Taiwanese politics and the democracy movement, women sharing family matters and offering mutual support. Children in the group grew up together and formed close, sibling-like bonds.
